text:
mel (acct-mgr): Customer on plan 'Growth' started hitting 400s for function calls after yesterday's deploy, says their tool 'translateText' suddenly fails. stacktrace attached.
elaine (support): Can you paste the error snippet? 400 is usually schema validation or missing tool.
mel (acct-mgr): Here's the log they sent:

```
POST /v1/tools/call
Body: {"tool":"translateText","args":{"text":"hola","target_lang":"en"}}
Response: 400 Bad Request
{"error":"tool not found or args invalid","code":"tool_lookup_failed"}
```

mel (acct-mgr): They swear it worked on Monday, nothing changed on their side.
elaine (support): @sam any registry/rename work yesterday that could cause alias drift?
sam (eng-api): We did a small rename for consistency: internal id stayed same but primary alias changed from `translateText` -> `translate-text` around 2067889000. It was behind a feature flag but rolled to prod for a subset of regions. Could be registry sync lag with client caches.
raj (devex): That explains casing/format issues. Some clients call by original alias; our lookup should consider legacy aliases but there's a TTL on alias propagation. Do you have the client's tenant id?
mel (acct-mgr): tenant: acct-98765. Customer provided curl repro, forwarded: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/tools/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"translateText","args":{"text":"hola","target_lang":"en"}}'
```

sam (eng-api): Running lookup logs for acct-98765: 
```
[2067889901] lookup: incoming alias="translateText" tenant=acct-98765 -> resolver: alias not found in cache
[2067889902] registry-querier: fallback query -> returned: aliases=["translate-text","translate_text"] primary="translate-text"
[2067889903] selector: alias TTL differs across regions: us-west=3600s, eu-central=0s
[2067889904] result: mismatch -> respond with 400 and code tool_lookup_failed
```

elaine (support): So their request hit a region where cache hadn't been updated and we didn't fallback to legacy alias. Do we have a quick mitigation for them?
sam (eng-api): Short-term: ask them to call the primary alias `translate-text` or we can patch the request on our side if they want a hotfix. Also we can flush alias cache for their tenant in eu-central.
mel (acct-mgr): Customer says they can't change client yet (heavy mobile rollout). They want us to fix.
registry-bot: [2067890200] ACTION: queued registry refresh for tenant acct-98765 in eu-central by support.
sam (eng-api): I'll trigger a targeted alias propagation and TTL reset. Commands I'll run: 
```
# internal
redwood-admin registry refresh --tenant acct-98765 --region eu-central --force
redwood-admin cache flush --keys alias:acct-98765:* --region eu-central
```

sam (eng-api): Followups: also adding compatibility layer to try case-insensitive and legacy aliases for 30 minutes for affected tenants so we don't rely on clients changing instantly.
elaine (support): Noted. I'll tell the customer we queued a region-specific refresh and ask them to retry in ~2 mins.
mel (acct-mgr): Customer retried after 3 mins and reports success. They received 200 and translation result. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [2067890400] deploy: feature/alias-compatibility rolled out (canary)
raj (devex): We should add an alert when alias primary changes are published: owners must confirm propagation to all regions or a grace alias mapping created. Filing a follow-up RFC.
mel (acct-mgr): Customer happy for now, requested postmortem and guarantee this won't recur on next rename.
elaine (support): I'll open a PM-ticket for postmortem and link to this thread. Action items: 1) Sam to keep compatibility fallback for 30m + PR to increase alias propagation visibility. 2) Raj to write RFC for rename process. 3) Support to confirm customer SLA credit if needed.
sam (eng-api): Will post PR and changelog. Also recommending we normalize alias matching: casefold + punctuation-insensitive match internally.
elaine (support): Thanks team — closing incident after postmortem.
mel (acct-mgr): Closing with customer note: "We applied a fix on our side and you should be good to continue. We'll follow up with process changes."
